region_scene_page.compact: After the 1990s country boom, Nashville radio kept scaling up, absorbing pop, rock, and hip-hop production habits while preserving enough country codes for format identity.
region_scene_page.standard: After the 1990s country boom, Nashville radio kept scaling up, absorbing pop, rock, and hip-hop production habits while preserving enough country codes for format identity. Keith Urban's Days Go By, Miranda Lambert's Gunpowder & Lead, Eric Church's Drink in My Hand, and Carrie Underwood's Blown Away give the scene its high-recognition landmarks.
region_scene_page.deep: After the 1990s country boom, Nashville radio kept scaling up, absorbing pop, rock, and hip-hop production habits while preserving enough country codes for format identity. The songs are loud, bright, hook-heavy, and often built for trucks, tailgates, arenas, and playlists. Keith Urban's Days Go By, Miranda Lambert's Gunpowder & Lead, Eric Church's Drink in My Hand, and Carrie Underwood's Blown Away give the scene its high-recognition landmarks. From there, the examples move from quick recognition toward medium and deeper scene signals.
